content.text:
## Answer

The machine-wide mutex is the `BenchMutex` class in **`src/agentic_hil/bench.py`**.

Key details:

- **`BenchMutex`** (`src/agentic_hil/bench.py`, class defined around line ~328) represents "one owner's hold on a set of physical devices." It maintains an in-process record of held devices (`_held: dict[str, _HeldDevice]`) and takes real OS-level locks per resource (via file locks under a `device_lock_root()`, using `fcntl.flock`/`msvcrt.locking`-style primitives seen in the `_LifetimeLock`/lock-file machinery in the same file).
- Its `acquire()` method takes every named physical resource all-or-nothing, in sorted order, raising `DeviceBusyError` naming the current holder if another process already holds one of the resources — this is exactly what stops two processes from driving the same probe/board/port at once.
- `acquire_named()` is used for the special enumeration pseudo-resource (`debugger-discovery:all`) to serialize probe enumeration itself across the whole machine.
- Resource *names* locked by the mutex (e.g. `probe:<serial>`, `com:serial:<serial_number>`, `com:<device>`, `physical:<resource_id>`, `can:<adapter>:<channel>`) are computed per device kind in **`src/agentic_hil/devices.py`**, via each `Device` subclass's `lock_key`/`lock_keys` property (e.g. `UartDevice.lock_key`, `DebuggerDevice.lock_keys`). The `Device.acquire`/`DeviceSet.acquire` methods (also in `devices.py`) are documented as "the only way a device is taken," and they delegate straight into `BenchMutex.acquire`.

So conceptually:
- **`devices.py`** decides *what* hardware identity/name to lock (probe serial, COM port serial/device path, CAN adapter+channel).
- **`bench.py`**'s `BenchMutex` is the actual machine-wide exclusion mechanism (backed by OS file locks) that enforces only one process/owner can hold a given resource name at a time, raising `DeviceBusyError` naming the holder on conflict.

Additionally, for serial ports specifically, there's a second, complementary safeguard at the OS level: `src/agentic_hil/comports.py` sets `serial_handle.exclusive = True` when opening a port (POSIX `O_EXCL`-style exclusive open), explicitly noted in comments there as covering the case of "a foreign test runner or serial monitor" that the `BenchMutex` (which only binds cooperating `agentic-hil` runs) cannot protect against.
